thread.title: Will FAANG Stocks Remain The Market's Heartbeat In 2019?

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Will FAANG Stocks Remain The Market's Heartbeat In 2019?
text:
Shutterstock photo Tech stocks in 2018 didn't duplicate the better-than-38% gain they posted as a group in 2017 when the sector was boosted by the power of "FAANG" — Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Apple ( AAPL ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Google parent Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ). There’s no question these five superpowers, which have been on a sustained rally the last five years, were the heartbeat of the stock market.
In 2018? Not so much. In fact, some have argued that FAANGs, particularly in the last three months of the year when they lost a combined $1 trillion in value in the recent rout, were the cause of many broken portfolios. The privacy concerns that plagued Facebook and Google resulted in respective declines of 26% and 2% in 2018. Meanwhile, Apple has lost 7% year to date, including 30% in three months on fears of lower iPhone sales.
Though Netflix will end 2018 up nearly 40%, it has also lost 30% of its value in the last three months amid concerns of decelerating subscriber growth. If not for Amazon (up 30% in 2018) the axiom of “ live by the FAANG, die by the FAANG ,” would have proven true. Can the group bounce back in 2019? If so, what will it take?
Veteran trader Art Cashin of UBS believes FAANGs remain an important, if not critical piece of the stock market. In an appearance on CNBC’s "Squawk on the Street,” Cashin said the FAANGs need to be "unified and consistent” if the markets are going to head higher.
Not everyone agrees that unity and consistency among the FAANGs is possible.
"Each of these stocks, going forward, are going to trade on their own footing and not as a group," said Peter Boockvar of Bleakley Advisory Group. Boockvar, who declared the FAANG trade "dead," is one of several analysts who are advising caution heading into 2019.
We entered 2018 with warnings that FAANGs were the most crowded trade on the market. To some extent, 2018’s tech outcome has given credence to that theory. But here’s the thing: for investors who are looking for bounce-back trade, wouldn’t it make sense that the reverse is now true for 2019 for the FAANGs? Perhaps the trade is no longer as crowded as it was once believed to be. And it’s highly likely that for this reason, among others, techs will regain its place as a market sector leader.
Consider that despite the fact tech stocks ended 2018 in the red, down 2.5%, the sector was nonetheless one of the better-performing groups, especially when compared to the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 Index, which both lost more than 6%. In terms of the FAANGs, sure, they have been punished in 2018. But aide from modestly trimming their price targets, the overwhelming majority of Wall Street analysts following each stock have stuck with their Buy ratings.
There were several times in the last five years when it was easy to buy into the notion that all FAANG stocks were expensive. That’s not the case in 2019. While I won’t go out on the limb (at least not yet) to call a stock market bottom, it’s an easy call to say that buying the FAANGs at current levels will be a profitable trade for throughout 2019. And they won’t need to be the heartbeat of the market, just that of my portfolio.
